disposition_reason: The 25th ATDS analysed 'Chocolate, milk' (4 composites) for total As, Cd, Pb and total Hg: Cd and Pb detected in all composites, total As and total Hg not detected. Inorganic As and Hg species were analysed only in seafood/rice/sushi, not chocolate.

study.growing_origin_vs_market: Purchase market Australia (four states/territories); cocoa growing origin not reported
study.sampling_unit: composite samples, each of three primary retail purchases from one state/territory
study.method: ICP-MS after acid digestion (Symbio Laboratories, NATA-accredited)

lod_loq.note: LOR = LOD; LOQ = 5 x LOD (Table 2 footnote)

notes: Out-of-scope cocoa-containing foods also tabulated: 'Cake, chocolate, iced' and 'Hot chocolate beverage' (made up as directed on label using tap water, or light milk if label specifies; i.e. a drink as consumed, not powder). Main report Tables 6 and 7 quote external comparators for milk chocolate (Cd mean nd=LOR: 23rd ATDS 0.042, US FDA 0.021, EFSA 0.021, NZ 0.039 mg/kg; Pb: 23rd ATDS 0.028, US FDA 0.011 [LB], EFSA 0.039, NZ 0.027 [middle bound] mg/kg); these are secondary citations, not 25th ATDS measurements. 'Chocolates and fudge' was a minor contributor to lead exposure for all ages except teenagers 13-18 (5%) (main report PDF p.51).
contradictions_with_stored_summary: Stored summary lists chocolate among foods with Cd detected in all composites but gives no milk chocolate concentration values (Cd 0.015, Pb 0.006 mg/kg); it reports chocolate cake values only.
unresolved: Which four states/territories supplied the milk chocolate composites is not stated.
